proof:
Source: step 0 of the parent proof (the supplied proof of dimred_mbl_dt_cube_bv_median): "for every constant β and admissible g, ∫_{Q₁} β div g = 0 (integrate each ∂_i g_i along coordinate lines; g has compact support in Q₁)". It is proved here for C¹ fields; the line integration is written as an integration by parts on ℝⁿ, and the coordinate-line version is given as an alternative in step 2. In Simon this is the fact, implicit in displays (29)–(30) of the proof of Ch. 6, 5.1 (book/chapter-06.txt lines 1862–1876), that subtracting the constant multiple β[[F]] does not change the boundary inside F̊.

Notation (used throughout). m ∈ ℕ and n := m + 1 ≥ 1. ℝⁿ means Euclid n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) with its Lebesgue measure (volume); y_i is the i-th coordinate and e_1, …, e_n is the standard orthonormal basis. Q₁ := {y : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i}; for δ ∈ ℝ, Q_δ := {y : δ < y_i < 1 − δ for all i} (so Q_0 = Q₁). div G(x) := trace DG(x) (LinearMap.trace of fderiv ℝ G x, viewed as a linear map). For v : ℝⁿ → ℝ, ‖Dv(x)‖ is the operator norm of fderiv ℝ v x, which equals the Euclidean length |∇v(x)| of the gradient. Integrals over a set are Bochner integrals for the restricted Lebesgue measure. Under the measure-preserving, coordinate-preserving continuous linear equivalence WithLp.ofLp : Euclid n ≃ (Fin n → ℝ) (Mathlib PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp / EuclideanSpace.volume_preserving_symm_measurableEquiv_toLp; it is not an isometry for the sup norm of Fin n → ℝ, and no isometry property is used) Q_δ corresponds to the box ∏_i (δ, 1 − δ); hence vol(Q_δ) = (1 − 2δ)ⁿ for 0 ≤ δ < 1/2, vol(Q₁) = 1, and Q_δ = ∅ for δ ≥ 1/2. Each Q_δ is open, convex and bounded, and Q_δ ⊆ Q_δ' ⊆ Q₁ for 0 ≤ δ' ≤ δ. "hyp(u, V)" abbreviates: ∫_{Q₁} u · div g ≤ V for every C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞)) map g : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ with compact support, tsupport g ⊆ Q₁ and |g(y)| ≤ 1 for all y.

Let g be C¹ with compact support, and put K := tsupport g, a compact subset of Q₁.

1. Regularity. Dg : ℝⁿ → L(ℝⁿ, ℝⁿ) is continuous because g is C¹. Moreover Dg(x) = 0 for x ∉ K: such an x has the open neighbourhood ℝⁿ ∖ K on which g ≡ 0 (Mathlib support_fderiv_subset: support (fderiv ℝ g) ⊆ tsupport g). Hence for each fixed h ∈ ℝⁿ the map x ↦ Dg(x)h is continuous with support in the compact set K, so it is integrable on ℝⁿ; likewise g is continuous with compact support, hence integrable. The map A ↦ trace A is linear on the finite-dimensional space L(ℝⁿ, ℝⁿ), hence continuous, so x ↦ div g(x) is continuous, vanishes outside K and is integrable on ℝⁿ.

2. Directional derivatives integrate to zero. Fix h ∈ ℝⁿ. Apply integration by parts on ℝⁿ (Mathlib integral_smul_fderiv_eq_neg_fderiv_smul_of_integrable, Lebesgue measure on Euclid n) to the scalar function f ≡ 1 and the vector function g in the direction h. Its hypotheses hold: x ↦ Df(x)h • g(x) = 0 is integrable; x ↦ f(x) • Dg(x)h = Dg(x)h is integrable by step 1; x ↦ f(x) • g(x) = g(x) is integrable by step 1; f is differentiable everywhere; g is differentiable everywhere (C¹). It gives ∫_{ℝⁿ} Dg(x)h dx = −∫_{ℝⁿ} Df(x)h • g(x) dx = −∫ 0 = 0. Import note: this lemma lives in Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.LineDeriv.IntegrationByParts, which is not in the import closure of the frozen GMT/Ch07/Submission.lean; add `import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.LineDeriv.IntegrationByParts` to Submission.lean. Adding Mathlib imports to GMT/Ch07/Submission.lean is accepted practice in this run (29 accepted nodes do so, e.g. 10 import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Function.ContinuousMapDense and 10 import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.BumpFunction.SmoothApprox); the challenge and the solution of the child comparator both import the candidate Submission, so the frozen type is unaffected. Alternative route inside the closure, needed only for h = e_i in step 3: identify Euclid n with Fin n → ℝ (PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp) and split off coordinate i (MeasureTheory.volume_preserving_piFinSuccAbove, x = Fin.insertNth i t x'); by Fubini ∫_{ℝⁿ} ∂_i g_k = ∫_{x'} (∫_ℝ (d/dt) g_k(Fin.insertNth i t x') dt) dx', and for each x' the inner integral vanishes by MeasureTheory.integral_eq_zero_of_hasDerivAt_of_integrable (t ↦ g_k(Fin.insertNth i t x') is C¹ with compact support, so it and its derivative are integrable on ℝ).

3. Trace in the standard basis. For every linear T : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ, trace T = Σ_i ⟨e_i, T e_i⟩ (Mathlib LinearMap.trace_eq_sum_inner with the orthonormal basis EuclideanSpace.basisFun). Hence div g(x) = Σ_i ⟨e_i, Dg(x)e_i⟩ for every x. Since v ↦ ⟨e_i, v⟩ is a continuous linear functional and x ↦ Dg(x)e_i is integrable, ∫_{ℝⁿ} ⟨e_i, Dg(x)e_i⟩ dx = ⟨e_i, ∫_{ℝⁿ} Dg(x)e_i dx⟩ = ⟨e_i, 0⟩ = 0 by step 2 (ContinuousLinearMap.integral_comp_comm for innerSL ℝ e_i). Summing over i (integral of a finite sum of integrable functions): ∫_{ℝⁿ} div g = 0.

4. Restriction to Q₁. By step 1, div g vanishes outside K ⊆ Q₁, so ∫_{Q₁} div g = ∫_{ℝⁿ} div g (Mathlib setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero, applied to the integrand that vanishes off Q₁). By step 3 this is 0. ∎
key_steps: Dg is continuous and vanishes off tsupport g ⊆ Q₁, so g, every Dg(·)h and div g are integrable on ℝⁿ.
Integration by parts against the constant function 1 (or FTC along coordinate lines) gives ∫_{ℝⁿ} Dg(x)h dx = 0 for every direction h.
div g = Σ_i ⟨e_i, Dg e_i⟩, so ∫_{ℝⁿ} div g = Σ_i ⟨e_i, ∫ Dg e_i⟩ = 0.
div g vanishes off Q₁, so ∫_{Q₁} div g = ∫_{ℝⁿ} div g = 0.
